business.body: The Company crushes sugarcane sourced from its reserved command zone in Uttar Pradesh to manufacture sugar, with molasses and bagasse arising as by-products. Bagasse is used to fire a high-pressure cogeneration power plant whose surplus power is exported to Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL), while the Spirits division distils molasses into RS/SDS/Ethanol. The Company has no subsidiary, associate company or joint venture company, and there was no change in the nature of its business during the year under review.

outlook.body:
- Improve the cane price payment cycle to farmers in the reserved command zone — management states cane diversion to neighbouring factories will keep rising unless the payment position improves, and says it has been making efforts to improve its payment position in relation to cane dues so that it may perform better in the coming year
- Strengthen agronomic practices and farmer relationship management within the command zone to defend cane availability against a new sugar mill coming up within 15 km
- Keep the cogeneration power plant synchronised with sugar plant operations only, and stay shut during the off-season while power tariffs remain unviable
- Keep the distillery shut until the molasses cost / RS-SDS-Ethanol realisation spread improves, with a restart call to be taken on market dynamics by end September/October 2026
- Advocate at industry level for a revision of the sugar Minimum Selling Price in line with FRP increases and adoption of the Rangarajan Committee 'linkage formula' tying cane price to sugar realisation
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company discloses no new expansion project for FY 2025-26. The one named project in the bundle is the 80 KLPD expansion, for which orders had been issued to M/s. Mojj Engineering Systems P Ltd for execution and to Avant-Garde Systems & Controls (P) Ltd as consultant, and which had been carried as a capital commitment of Rs. 2,997.37 lakhs during FY 2024-25; owing to indefinite deferment of this project it is no longer considered a capital commitment. Operationally, the existing asset base was run below its potential rather than expanded: the cogeneration power plant was run at lower capacity because of reduced cane availability and was shut immediately after the close of sugar plant operations rather than run through the off-season, on account of reduced and unviable power tariffs; the distillery was not operated at all during FY 2025-26. The Company states it did not raise any funds by issue of equity shares or debt securities during FY 2025-26 and obtained no fresh credit facilities from any bank or financial institution.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Sugar price outlook for FY 2026-27 expected to be steady, supported by low opening stock levels and the possibility of reduced cane availability
- The Government's current restriction/ban on sugar exports is expected to support domestic sugar prices and improve industry margins
- Management expects these factors collectively to result in the Company generating better operational margins gradually; the industry outlook is described as positive in the short and long term with sugar prices expected to be encouraging and stable
- Sugar recovery improved to 10.23% in SS 2025-26 from 9.55% in SS 2024-25, cushioning sugar output despite a lower cane crush
- Cane availability is the binding constraint: cane area fell from 27,012 hectares in SS 2024-25 to 18,636 hectares in SS 2025-26 on delayed cane payments, and a new mill within 15 km adds structural competitive pressure
- UP's SAP-based cane pricing (Rs. 390-400 per quintal against FRP of Rs. 354.23 at the Company's 10.23% recovery, a premium of Rs. 45.77 per quintal) leaves UP mills with the highest production costs in India and structurally less competitive than Maharashtra and Karnataka mills
- Sugar MSP unchanged at Rs. 31.00 per kg for over six years despite significant increases in FRP and input costs, sustaining pressure on mill realisations
- Power division revenue visibility from UPERC's revised tariff of Rs. 4.43 per unit for FY 2025-26 (from Rs. 3.46 earlier) under a multi-year tariff framework effective 1st April 2024; off-season operation remains unviable at prevailing tariffs
- Spirits division economics blocked by molasses at Rs. 1,000-1,100 per quintal against RS/SDS selling prices of Rs. 50 or below; an improvement in ethanol blending mandates and Government ethanol pricing would be the trigger for resumption
- Global backdrop is bearish — USDA projects 2025/26 world production of ~189.3 million metric tons against consumption of ~178.1 million metric tons, a surplus and rising ending stocks that may limit India's export window
